item: Distinct Tor isolation tokens ask for distinct circuits: Wikidata lookups, statistics pages and download segments no longer share one (queue item 50(a))
summary: Queue item 50(a), an R621 follow-up recorded by Export with no PR planned; taken at the coordinator's request after #1913. BEFORE: src.safety.fetcher._with_stream_isolation named a token's Tor circuit (Tor's IsolateSOCKSAuth builds one circuit per SOCKS credential) by the token stripped to [A-Za-z0-9_.-] and cut at 32 characters, so tokens that agreed on their first 32 kept characters shared one credential and one circuit, against the claims of their callers; a name with no kept character (a Unicode token) read 'oo', and host:port read the same as hostport. NOW: _isolation_credential(token) uses a token as written when it is at most 32 characters of [A-Za-z0-9_.-] (a host key, dl-1: unchanged), and names any other token by 'oo.' and the first 32 hex digits of the HMAC-SHA256 of the WHOLE token (UTF-8, a lone surrogate passed through) under a 32-byte key that secrets.token_bytes makes once per process and that is held only in memory (35 characters, so it can never equal an as-written credential). It is keyed because a plain digest of a URL lets whoever reads the SOCKS handshake (the proxy, a Tor control-port reader) hash a guessed lookup and confirm it. The same token keeps its credential for the life of the process and gets another after a restart; credentials a caller set and non-SOCKS proxies are left alone as before; a URL token's path and query no longer reach the proxy URL (they used to, cut at 32). WHAT IT CHANGES, measured with the callers' own URL builders, credentials before and after: 30 Wikidata lookups (wikidata_rings.wbsearch_url and wbentities_url; the ring loader's and the catalogue apply's docstrings say each lookup rides its own circuit) 1 and 30; the HEAD and 4 segments of one dump (segmented_download.default_fetch_segment's url#seg-a-b tokens, whose docstring says each segment rides its own circuit) 1 and 5; the three dump kinds of one wiki 1 and 3; World Bank, one indicator's 18 pages 1 and 18, and 36 indicators' 648 pages 1 and 648 (src/stats/fetch.py says it gives per-URL isolation to every page; a walk stops at _WORLDBANK_MAX_PAGES = 200); Eurostat's 3 datasets 1 and 3; OSM replication of one region, its state file and 90 diffs, 1 and 91; self-update's two GitHub reads 1 and 2. So a paginated statistics walk and a replication catch-up now build one circuit per request, as their callers asked; no caller was changed, and whether such a walk should share one circuit per query is put to the owning lanes as a follow-up. The 9 OSM region URLs already gave 9, and the 5,540 hosts of the 9 bundled catalogues counted (sources, academic, official, legal, legal generated, calendar feeds, markets, commodity feeds, index feeds) already gave 5,540 per-host credentials and keep them. TESTS: tests/test_isolation_credential_item50.py, 21: the callers' own URL builders; the segmented download's own fetch and the four Wikidata getters (ring loader, catalogue apply, entities items, gazetteer build) with guarded_session replaced, each of which must hand over the URL it asks for; the fetcher's own per-host proxies; a protected-mode guarded_session over one SOCKS proxy; the keyed digest under a fixed probe key; a fresh key in each of two interpreters; and a large set of real tokens. On 1d1204bfd 17 fail and the 4 that pin unchanged behaviour pass. MUTANTS: 14, all killed (8 on the first build: the as-written bound raised, a digest of the first 32 characters, of the stripped token, without the prefix, shortened, no character check, search for fullmatch, the old rule back; 6 on the fold: a fixed key, a plain SHA-256, strict UTF-8, a keyed digest of the first 32 characters, a constant token in the ring loader, and in the gazetteer build). READS: two independent security reads of the first build. One must-fix (the unkeyed digest let a guessed lookup be confirmed), folded as the per-process key; should-fixes, folded (the Wikidata test did not drive the callers, the query test passed for the wrong reason, and the surrogate path and a protected-mode session with a digest credential were untested). NOT CHANGED, stated: Tor decides what a circuit is, and this only makes distinct tokens ask for distinct circuits; IsolateSOCKSAuth must be on in the operator's Tor (it is by default); an HTTP proxy still cannot isolate. A circuit is not the whole of linkability: the Wikidata lookups carry the app's one honest User-Agent and their timing, so the 'unlinkable over Tor' wording in ring_loader.py and wikidata_apply.py says more than circuits give. The segments of one download now leave by several exits, each seeing its own byte range; the segmented path runs only for an entry that carries mirrors or an expected SHA-256, which no shipped entry does, and only on a fresh start. The mirror probe's timed HEAD now rides another circuit than the segments it chooses for. PySocks, which socks5h:// needs, is not in pyproject or the lock (pre-existing). Release-notes line: «Over Tor, each Wikidata lookup, each page of statistics and each segment of a download now rides its own circuit, as the app already said; before, requests to one site could share one.»
